description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 (%) on geometry problems (Geomverse) and the number of child nodes (tree width) for rollout search, comparing two large vision-language models: GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width),” is linearly scaled from 1 to 7 with integer tick marks at each unit. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)”, ranges from 15 to 35 with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 5. The GPT-4o model is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; its accuracy starts at 24.4% at tree width 1, rises to 28.9% at width 3, peaks at 34.4% at width 5, then declines to 31.1% at width 7. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet model is shown as a solid light purple line with cross markers; it begins at 26.7% at width 1, slightly increases to 27.8% at width 3, then steadily decreases to 24.4% at width 5 and further drops to 20.0% at width 7. While GPT-4o exhibits an inverted U-shaped performance trend peaking at tree width 5, Claude-3.5-Sonnet shows a generally declining trend after an initial slight rise, maintaining higher accuracy than GPT-4o at widths 1 and 3, but falling below it at widths 5 and 7.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
